t: Section 1650 of the Internal Revenue Code (war tax rates of certain miscellaneous taxes) is hereby amended by striking out “and ending on the first day of the first month which begins six months or more after the date of the termination of hostilities in the present war”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Internal Revenue Code by striking a phrase that tied war tax rates to the end of hostilities. There is no tempting participation reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a direct legislative amendment to the Internal Revenue Code regarding tax rates. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. It simply changes the statutory text.
qwen_block.s: Section 1650 of the Internal Revenue Code (war tax rates of certain miscellaneous taxes) is hereby amended by striking out “and ending on the first day of the first month which begins six months or more after the date of the termination of hostilities in the present war”.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tax rates affects the public, so it involves participation. However, the definition requires a specific mechanism for outside parties to consult, coordinate, or provide input *before* a decision is made. This section is a direct legislative amendment to a statute, not a procedural requirement for public input.

opus.w: The section only strikes a time-limiting phrase from the war tax rate provision of the Internal Revenue Code. It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of the 'termination of hostilities' just fixes a date and gives no outside party a role in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code by removing a specific date limitation for war tax rates. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, public hearings, or advisory committees involving non-federal members. It is a substantive legislative change, not a procedural requirement for participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1650 of the Internal Revenue Code (war tax rates of certain miscellaneous taxes) is hereby amended by striking out “and ending on the first day of the first month which begins six months or more after the date of the termination of hostilities in the present war”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tax rates affects the public, so it involves participation. However, the definition requires a specific procedural mechanism (consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory board with outsiders, right to sue) where outsiders are involved *before* a federal decision is made. This section is a substantive amendment to tax law, not a procedural requirement for public input.
